annotations.guideline_section: A textual string may refer to a disease name, but it may modify a noun phrase (or may not be a noun phrase itself). In such cases, annotate using the Modifier category.

annotations.rationale: This is the full name of a single recognized disorder, headed by 'deficiency' and taking the specific enzyme G6PD as its complement; it is used in a prevalence/disease context, not merely as a lab abnormality.
annotations.guideline_section: IF a noun phrase is headed by a deficit/absence nominalization or reduced-function expression and takes a complement naming a specific molecular entity (e.g., an enzyme, gene, or protein), and the phrase is used in a disease-denoting frame such as definition, causation, characterization, or responsibility for a clinical condition, THEN annotate the whole phrase as SpecificDisease; DO NOT apply this rule when the same wording refers only to an isolated biochemical finding, mechanistic description, or laboratory abnormality rather than the disorder itself.
